results.Notes: Closest comparators: MA-Q-0230 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-PRECEPTOR-INTERN-RATIO), MA-Q-0077 (prior bank, intern supervision) and MA-Q-0231 (B3-A sibling, support-personnel ratio). Competing reasoning path: the manager invites the candidate to reason from the 247 CMR 8.06(3) support-personnel ratio, which genuinely has headroom, while the controlling limit is the separate preceptor cap in 247 CMR 8.01(16). Materially distinct: MA-Q-0077 tests whether an intern may work at all without a preceptor directing the work and never reaches the numeric preceptor cap; MA-Q-0230 runs the intern's authority downward toward technicians rather than the preceptor's capacity upward; MA-Q-0231 turns on credential composition inside the 8.06(3) ratio, which is the very rule this item asks the candidate to set aside. No prior bank item tests the two-intern cap.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0229 (B3-A sibling, same rule), MA-Q-0077 (prior bank, intern supervision) and MA-Q-0075 (prior bank, trainee duties under direct supervision). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must decide whether an intern's own supervised status disqualifies the intern from supervising others, which 247 CMR 8.01(15) resolves the other way by making that supervised status the precondition. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0077 keys on the intern needing a preceptor and on intern status not authorising independent pharmacist practice, both upward-facing propositions, whereas this item is the only bank item on the intern's downward authority over pharmacy technicians. MA-Q-0075 concerns what a trainee may do, not who may supervise a technician.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0232 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-SUPPORT-PERSONNEL-RATIO), MA-Q-0233 (B3-A sibling, ratio consequence of a lapsed certification) and MA-Q-0076 (prior bank, Schedule II technician pathways). Competing reasoning path: the item punishes headcount thinking, because four support personnel is available only on one of three credential-composition clauses in 247 CMR 8.06(3)(a)1, and options C, D and E each present a lawful-looking four-person shift that satisfies none of them. Materially distinct: no prior bank item tests the ratio at all; MA-Q-0232 tests exclusion of non-support staff from the same ratio rather than its composition clauses, and MA-Q-0233 tests the downstream effect of a certification lapse on an already-formed shift.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0231 (B3-A sibling, same rule), MA-Q-0229 (B3-A sibling, competing supervisory limit) and MA-Q-0247 (B3-A sibling, Manager of Record duties). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must see that 247 CMR 8.06(3)(b) excludes by function rather than by title, so the cashier's exclusion survives only while the cashier gives no professional support. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0231 asks which credential mixes unlock a four-person ratio and assumes the population is already support personnel, whereas this item asks who enters the population at all. No prior bank item addresses the 8.06(3)(b) exclusion.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0246 (B3-A sibling, sharing rule MA-CERT-TECH-LAPSE), MA-Q-0231 (B3-A sibling, the ratio the lapse feeds into) and MA-Q-0076 (prior bank, certified versus non-certified technician pathways). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must keep the certifying body's certification and the Board licence apart, then carry the lapse through to scope, title and the supervisory-ratio count. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0076 distinguishes certified from non-certified technicians only for Schedule II assistance and never addresses lapse; MA-Q-0246 takes the same lapse to the single question of the name tag. Noted weakness rather than a criterion failure: distractors D and E are the two weakest options because the stem's statement that the Board licence remains current already undercuts them, so the item's real discrimination rests on recognising the ratio consequence in option C.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0235 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-CERT-TECH-SCOPE), MA-Q-0236 (B3-A sibling, plain technician telephone authority) and MA-Q-0140 (prior bank, certified-technician ADD stocking). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must classify omitted directions as relayed information rather than an exercise of professional judgment, then apply the two conditions of self-identification and pharmacist-on-duty approval. Materially distinct: the prior bank's certified-technician items are all automated-dispensing-device stocking questions under MA-ADD-TECH and never reach 247 CMR 8.04(4)(c) telephone communication; MA-Q-0235 is the transfer limb of the same subsection and MA-Q-0236 is the narrower authority of an uncertified technician.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0234 (B3-A sibling, same rule), MA-Q-0120 (prior bank, prescription transfer requirements) and MA-Q-0019 (prior bank, electronic controlled-prescription transfer). Competing reasoning path: the pharmacist's willingness to approve is a genuine attractor, and the candidate must see that approval is a precondition to a narrow Schedule VI authority rather than a means of widening it. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0120 and MA-Q-0019 test transfer mechanics such as refills remaining and transfer counts and are silent on who may execute a transfer, whereas this item is a personnel-authority question. Not a schedule flashcard: the Massachusetts Schedule VI boundary is the operative scope limit on a delegated act, not a recall target, and option E is defeated because in Massachusetts a non-controlled prescription drug is itself a Schedule VI substance.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0234 (B3-A sibling, certified-technician communication authority), MA-Q-0237 (B3-A sibling, trainee telephone bar) and MA-Q-0075 (prior bank, trainee clinical boundary). Competing reasoning path: the pharmacist's prior approval of the refill call is a strong attractor, and the candidate must recognise that the approval is bounded by the unchanged-information proviso, which the dose increase breaks mid-call. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0075 tests counselling and unresolved drug utilisation review at pickup rather than telephone refill authority; MA-Q-0234 gives the certified technician a wider but still bounded authority. No prior bank item reaches 247 CMR 8.02(6)(c).

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0238 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-TECH-TRAINEE-LIMITS), MA-Q-0075 (prior bank, trainee duties under direct supervision) and MA-Q-0139 (prior bank, trainee stocking functions). Competing reasoning path: 247 CMR 8.03(4)(b) grants trainees pharmacy technician duties under direct supervision, and the candidate must notice that the same subsection carves the telephone out, so the staffing crunch and the supervision both fail to help. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0075 and MA-Q-0139 both test what a supervised trainee may do in dispensing and stocking workflows and neither touches telephone intake; MA-Q-0238 tests the employment-duration limit rather than task scope. Noted weakness rather than a criterion failure: four options are conditional permissions and the key is the single flat prohibition, a mild structural cue, but option A states the general grant accurately enough that a candidate who has not read 8.03(4)(c) will be drawn to it.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0237 (B3-A sibling, same rule), MA-Q-0239 (B3-A sibling, technician licence eligibility, which shares the 500-hour trainee figure) and MA-Q-0078 (prior bank, intern hour cap). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must apply the shorter-of-two-periods rule to 1520 hours in ten months and then decide which of four proposed escapes are among the three enumerated exceptions, with employer staffing pressure as the plausible but absent one. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0078 caps internship credit per day for a different licence type under a different rule; nothing in the prior bank addresses trainee employment duration or the 30-day post-eighteenth-birthday application duty.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0238 (B3-A sibling, 500-hour trainee threshold), MA-Q-0248 and MA-Q-0251 (B3-A siblings, pharmacist eligibility and reciprocity route structures). Competing reasoning path: the stem closes off every requirement except 247 CMR 8.02(3)(e), so the candidate must recognise the three routes as genuine alternatives, each independently sufficient, and reject an employer attestation and cashier service that resemble but do not satisfy them. Materially distinct: no prior bank item addresses technician licensure eligibility at all; MA-Q-0248 and MA-Q-0251 concern pharmacist examination and reciprocity pathways with different actors, credentials and conditions.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0254 (B3-A sibling, pharmacist personal registration lapse), MA-Q-0233 (B3-A sibling, credential lapse consequences) and MA-Q-0221 (prior bank, drug store pharmacy licence renewal cycle). Competing reasoning path: an intention to pay all back and late fees is the attractor, and the candidate must separate prospective restoration of the licence from the character of the shifts already worked. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0221 asks when a facility licence expires and is a cycle-arithmetic item about a different licensee; MA-Q-0254 concerns a pharmacist registration beyond two years and its MPJE consequence rather than the unlicensed-practice characterisation. No prior bank item covers 247 CMR 8.07.

Closest comparator: MA-Q-0076 (prior bank, Pharmacy personnel / Schedule II handling, rule MA-TECH-CII), which is the strongest lexical match to any B3-A item against the prior bank at cosine 0.60; further comparators are MA-Q-0231 and MA-Q-0233 (B3-A siblings) and MA-Q-0138 (prior bank, trainee stocking at a satellite clinic). Competing reasoning path: the item asks the candidate to grade transporting against handling across three technician grades while keeping accountability with the pharmacist. NOT materially distinct: three of the four keyed options restate keyed propositions of MA-Q-0076 almost one to one, since option A corresponds to MA-Q-0076 option E, option B to MA-Q-0076 option A and option C to MA-Q-0076 option C, and MA-Q-0076 already supplies the approved written policies and procedures of option D as a stem fact. A candidate who has mastered MA-Q-0076 obtains this item's keyed set without new reasoning. The genuinely new content is the false option E carrying the 247 CMR 8.05(3) hydrocodone-only extended release bar and its intern carve-out, which no prior item reaches, but that discrimination sits in a distractor and does not carry the item. Recommended minimum change: re-pitch the item so its keyed discrimination is the 8.05(3) bar and the intern carve-out rather than the 8.05(1) and 8.05(2) grading already covered by MA-Q-0076. The item is legally sound; this is a bank-redundancy finding only.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0103 (prior bank, licensee change reporting within 14 days), MA-Q-0243 (B3-A sibling, residency credential) and MA-Q-0230 (B3-A sibling, intern authority). Competing reasoning path: the intern's plan to reapply and her continued shifts invite the candidate to defer or reassign the duty, while 247 CMR 8.01(18) fixes it on her and triggers it on the withdrawal itself. Materially distinct despite the shared 14-day period: MA-Q-0103 concerns a licensed pharmacist reporting a name and address change under a different rule and a different trigger, and it does not raise the eligibility consequence that withdrawal carries for an intern licence under 247 CMR 8.01(2)(b). The overlap is a coincidence of period length, not of reasoning.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0244 (B3-A sibling, the other pre-internship credential gate), MA-Q-0242 and MA-Q-0230 (B3-A siblings on intern status) and MA-Q-0077 (prior bank, intern supervision). Competing reasoning path: a residency appointment and a PharmD look like practice authority, and the candidate must resolve 247 CMR 8.01(8)'s two named limbs and see that the pharmacist-licence limb is closed because neither examination has been passed. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0077 keys on an intern needing a preceptor in the abstract, whereas this item is the only bank item on the residency credential requirement; option C is a genuine trap because a pharmacist licence really is one of the two permitted arrangements, just not the available one.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0248 (B3-A sibling, foreign-graduate examination eligibility), MA-Q-0245 (B3-A sibling, internship composition) and MA-Q-0078 (prior bank, intern hours). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must separate the FPGEE authorization that gates entry to an internship from the FPGEC certification that gates examination eligibility, and must notice that the twenty-month age of the authorization defeats a currency requirement rather than an existence requirement. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0078 is a daily-credit item under a different rule, and MA-Q-0248 sits on the far side of the same candidate's journey at examination eligibility. The FPGEE-versus-FPGEC discrimination appears nowhere else in the bank.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0078 (prior bank, intern hours, the strongest prior match for this item), MA-Q-0244 (B3-A sibling, internship entry) and MA-Q-0229 (B3-A sibling, preceptor capacity). Competing reasoning path: the headline 1500 hours can be satisfied by a raw count that fails the internal 1000-hour and 500-hour composition, and the candidate must also reject a plausible single-calendar-year confinement that the regulation does not impose. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0078 tests only the 12-hour daily credit cap under 247 CMR 8.01(4) and says nothing about total hours, their composition, the experiential alternative or out-of-state credit. Reasoning rather than trivia: the numbers are the vehicle for a composition-versus-total distinction and a pathway-selection distinction.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0233 (B3-A sibling, sharing rule MA-CERT-TECH-LAPSE), MA-Q-0231 (B3-A sibling, ratio) and MA-Q-0240 (B3-A sibling, credential expiry). Competing reasoning path: the pharmacy's framing that it is merely sorting out paperwork invites leaving the tag alone, and the candidate must see that the displayed title must track the credential actually held while the tag itself stays mandatory. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0233 takes the same lapse to scope, title and ratio as a set, whereas this item isolates the identification duty and forces a choice among four wrong handlings including removing the tag altogether and demoting the individual to trainee. No prior bank item covers the name-tag rules.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0224 (prior bank, Pharmacy management / planned Manager of Record absence), MA-Q-0232 (B3-A sibling, support-personnel classification) and MA-Q-0233 (B3-A sibling). Competing reasoning path: never having filed the documents reads as a violation, and the candidate must recognise that 247 CMR 8.06(1) creates an availability-on-request duty rather than an advance-filing duty, so the correct response is production now. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0224 concerns notifying the Board about a temporary Manager of Record absence, a different duty with a different trigger and timetable; this is the only bank item on the support-personnel documentation duty, and option A is a strong attractor precisely because many Board duties are filing duties.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0244 (B3-A sibling, foreign-graduate internship entry), MA-Q-0251 (B3-A sibling, reciprocity requirements) and MA-Q-0245 (B3-A sibling, internship composition). Competing reasoning path: the two-applicant framing forces the candidate to find what the pathways share rather than how they differ, and the central trap is treating FPGEC certification as a substitute for the internship when it substitutes only for the accredited degree. Materially distinct: no prior bank item addresses pharmacist examination eligibility; MA-Q-0244 concerns the earlier FPGEE authorization gate for beginning an internship, which is a different document at a different stage.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0254 and MA-Q-0255 (B3-A siblings, other MPJE-triggering timetables) and MA-Q-0251 (B3-A sibling, reciprocity MPJE requirement). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must see that the one-year clock governs whether an already-passed NAPLEX score still counts alongside a later MPJE result, rather than governing the number of permitted retakes, which is what option B invites. Materially distinct: no prior bank item addresses examination scoring or retake linkage; the sibling items attach the MPJE to lapse and discipline ladders rather than to score pairing.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0251 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-LICENSURE-RECIPROCITY), MA-Q-0248 (B3-A sibling, examination eligibility) and MA-Q-0211 (prior bank, Board action classification). Competing reasoning path: NABP's role as the entity that issued the adverse notification makes appealing to NABP the natural first instinct, and the candidate must know NABP acts only as the Board's agent for the preliminary evaluation. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0251 enumerates substantive reciprocity requirements while this item is procedural and turns on the allocation of final authority; MA-Q-0211 concerns the disciplinary classification of a Board communication, not reciprocity review.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0250 (B3-A sibling, same rule), MA-Q-0248 (B3-A sibling, examination eligibility) and MA-Q-0239 (B3-A sibling, technician eligibility routes). Competing reasoning path: reciprocity feels like a transfer that should carry the applicant's prior jurisprudence credential with it, and the candidate must see that the internship documentation, the 75% MPJE and the possible personal appearance all survive. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0250 tests the procedural remedy after an adverse NABP notification rather than the substantive requirement set; nothing in the prior bank addresses reciprocity.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0254 and MA-Q-0255 (B3-A siblings, registration status changes), MA-Q-0211 (prior bank, disciplinary classification) and MA-Q-0212 (prior bank, impairment monitoring). Competing reasoning path: the word nondisciplinary invites the inference that retirement shields the licensee and guarantees a route back, and the candidate must hold both the preserved disciplinary power and the discretionary review of a reinstatement petition. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0211 classifies an advisory letter and MA-Q-0212 describes a monitoring programme; neither touches retired status, and no prior bank item reaches 247 CMR 3.04.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0255 (B3-A sibling, renewal after discipline), MA-Q-0254 (B3-A sibling, renewal after lapse) and MA-Q-0103 (prior bank, licensee reporting duties). Competing reasoning path: a disclosed out-of-state sanction ordinarily invites deferral, conditions or investigation, and the candidate must check the two qualifiers in 247 CMR 3.05 and then recognise that probation or deferral would be denial in substance. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0255 turns on the length of a Massachusetts suspension and its MPJE consequence, an entirely different mechanism; no prior bank item addresses protected health care activity. Practice plausibility is high given current interjurisdictional divergence, and the item stays on the licensure consequence rather than the clinical merits.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0255 (B3-A sibling, sharing rule MA-REGISTRATION-DISCIPLINE-REINSTATEMENT), MA-Q-0240 (B3-A sibling, technician licence lapse) and MA-Q-0221 (prior bank, facility licence renewal). Competing reasoning path: the two ladders in 247 CMR 4.02 look alike, and the candidate must place a 30-month lapse with no discipline on the failure-to-renew ladder rather than borrowing the NAPLEX possibility that belongs to the discipline ladder. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0255 starts from a disciplinary suspension and asks which band applies, the mirror question; MA-Q-0240 concerns a technician licence and the unlicensed-practice characterisation rather than the route back; MA-Q-0221 concerns a facility licence cycle.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0254 (B3-A sibling, same rule set), MA-Q-0253 (B3-A sibling, renewal and discipline) and MA-Q-0211 (prior bank, disciplinary classification). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must band a nine-month suspension between six months and two years and then resist importing the NAPLEX possibility that 247 CMR 4.02(7) reserves for the longer band, with option E testing whether serving the sanction is thought self-executing. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0254 approaches the same provision from a non-disciplinary lapse, and the two items key on different subsections with different consequences; MA-Q-0211 classifies a Board action rather than sequencing reinstatement.

Closest comparator: MA-Q-0079 (prior bank, Licensure / Continuing education, rule MA-PHARMACIST-CE), which is the single strongest B3-A to prior-bank lexical match in the tranche at cosine 0.78; further comparators are MA-Q-0257 and MA-Q-0258 (B3-A siblings) and MA-Q-0080 (prior bank, compounding CE). Competing reasoning path: the item asks the candidate to reject a cycle-total view of the 40 hours in favour of the per-calendar-year minimum. NOT materially distinct: MA-Q-0079 already tests exactly that discrimination, keying on the proposition that the 20-hour minimum applies to each calendar year, and its principal distractor is the same cycle-aggregate misconception. The two items are symmetric applications of one rule, MA-Q-0079 showing that a first-year surplus does not carry forward and this item showing that a first-year deficit cannot be cured later, and a candidate who masters either obtains the other without new reasoning. Both are Area 1, topic Licensure, single best answer, difficulty 5. The 30 hours of home study introduce a genuinely separate defect under the 15-hour annual cap in 247 CMR 4.03(4)(b), but the keyed answer does not rest on it, so it does not carry the item. Recommended minimum change: re-pitch the keyed discrimination onto the home-study cap already present in the fact pattern, which no bank item tests, or retire one of the two items. The item is legally sound; this is a bank-redundancy finding only.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0080 (prior bank, Licensure / Compounding CE, rule MA-CE-COMPOUNDING), MA-Q-0256 (B3-A sibling, annual CE structure) and MA-Q-0079 (prior bank, CE). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must map the fact pattern onto overlay triggers, accept the sterile and immunization overlays and the universal pharmacy law overlay, reject the complex non-sterile overlay whose trigger is absent, and reject doubling for satisfying two limbs of one overlay. Materially distinct despite the shared compounding CE subject: MA-Q-0080 keys on two compounding overlays both being triggered and stacking, and states its propositions without numbers, whereas this item keys on trigger selection across a different overlay set that MA-Q-0080 never reaches, adds the immunization overlay and the universal law overlay, carries the specific five, one and two hour values, and inverts MA-Q-0080's complex non-sterile proposition into a correctly excluded option. The two items are consistent rather than conflicting, since distinct overlays stack while one overlay is not doubled by two triggers.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0256 (B3-A sibling, sharing rule MA-CE-ANNUAL-STRUCTURE), MA-Q-0259 (B3-A sibling, sharing rule MA-CE-EXEMPTIONS) and MA-Q-0079 (prior bank, CE). Competing reasoning path: genuine hardship invites self-certification or a make-up period, and the candidate must recognise that relief is a Board determination on a sworn statement rather than a self-applied exemption. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0256 turns on the arithmetic of the annual minimum, MA-Q-0259 on an automatic statutory disapplication that requires no petition, and this item on the discretionary mechanism in between; MA-Q-0079 does not reach 247 CMR 4.03(6). Distractor D is well chosen because retired status is a real status that a candidate might misread as a parking place.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0258 (B3-A sibling, same rule MA-CE-EXEMPTIONS), MA-Q-0254 (B3-A sibling, registration validity) and MA-Q-0221 (prior bank, licence cycle arithmetic). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must combine a registration-validity limb measured from release from active duty with a continuing education limb that turns on the October 1st date condition, and must distinguish disapplication from deferral. Materially distinct: MA-Q-0258 is the discretionary hardship route requiring a sworn petition, whereas this relief operates automatically on dates; no prior bank item addresses military service. Practice plausibility is sound for a reserve or guard pharmacist, and the November entry date is doing real work rather than decorating the stem.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0256 and MA-Q-0258 (B3-A siblings, CE compliance) and MA-Q-0261 (B3-A sibling, provider-side CE administration). Competing reasoning path: the candidate must know that a bare attendance confirmation is insufficient and must identify the employer as the one plausible-sounding element that the regulation does not require. Materially distinct: no prior bank item addresses continuing education documentation content or the random-audit duty. Reasoning rather than trivia: the item is an applied sufficiency check against an enumerated list that a pharmacist must actually run at audit, and the discrimination sits in the excluded element rather than in recall of the included ones.

Closest comparators: MA-Q-0260 (B3-A sibling, CE administration), MA-Q-0250 (B3-A sibling, review of an adverse determination) and MA-Q-0072 and MA-Q-0090 (prior bank, closure-notice timing). Competing reasoning path: two 30-day periods sit in the same section and run from different events, so option A invites the candidate to treat the submission as timely and option E invites measuring the appeal from the presentation date. Materially distinct: the prior closure-notice items are advance-notice arithmetic for a pharmacy closing and involve no appeal right; MA-Q-0250 concerns Board review of an NABP determination on an individual reciprocity application rather than a provider's appeal from a designee's denial. No prior bank item reaches 247 CMR 4.04.
